candidate_name: Belco North Power Station LNG conversion (implied marine LNG import facility, no site named)
sponsor_or_proposer: Belco (Bermuda Electric Light Company) / Ascendant Group
current_state: Belco has repeatedly proposed converting/supplementing its North Power Station (commissioned 2020, designed dual-fuel oil/LNG-capable) to run on LNG, most recently developing a renewed LNG proposal (Royal Gazette, Jun 2023) and reported as 'desperately' wanting LNG use (Royal Gazette, Aug 2025). Belco's LNG proposal was rejected in the prior Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) process. Belco submitted its final draft 2026 IRP to the Regulatory Authority on 24 Jun 2026, but the whole future energy-planning process was suspended for up to 18 months by ministerial action in Jul 2026 (Royal Gazette). No marine LNG receiving facility (FSRU, ISO-container terminal, or onshore regas plant) has ever been named, sited, or permitted -- only the power-plant fuel-switch concept has been proposed, and even that is currently paused pending the suspended IRP review.
missing_threshold_elements: No terminal site or import-facility design identified (proposal is at the power-plant fuel-choice level, not a sited marine LNG receiving facility); concrete step actively blocked -- prior LNG IRP proposal was rejected by the regulator and the current planning process is suspended for up to 18 months.
watch_for: Resumption of Bermuda's energy planning process (currently suspended through ~early 2028) and any subsequent RA decision approving LNG for Belco; a named import-facility design (FSRU vs small-scale/ISO-container vs onshore terminal) and site would be the trigger to reconsider.
notes: Also: power-plant-fuel-choice != terminal (CLAUDE.md/SOP §3) -- even if approved, the LNG-receiving facility itself (not yet designed/sited) would be the terminal candidate, not the North Power Station. Do not stage as new_terminal.

candidate_name: Bullen Bay LNG Import Terminal (RdK-sponsored RFP, developer never selected)
sponsor_or_proposer: Refineria di Kòrsou (RdK) as offtaker/advisor (Poten & Partners); no LNG-terminal developer/owner ever publicly named
current_state: In 2016 RdK (advised by Poten & Partners) ran a tender inviting bidders to develop, finance, build, own and operate an LNG import terminal (FSRU or conventional onshore) at Bullen Bay, with a ~12.9 km pipeline to RdK's Willemstad refinery, targeting ~175 MMcf/d of domestic demand and an in-service date of 2021 or earlier (Offshore Energy, 2016). No winning bidder/developer was ever identified in any source found, no construction or FID news exists, and the target in-service year (2021) passed five years ago with no follow-up reporting located. The Curacao Isla refinery itself has been shuttered since 2019, and 2024-2026 reporting on its potential reopening (RdK/Curacao government seeking a new operator and US OFAC clearance to process Venezuelan crude) discusses only crude-oil feedstock, with no LNG/gas-supply component mentioned in any 2024-2026 source found.
missing_threshold_elements: Sponsor test fails for the actual terminal (RdK is the demand-side pipeline offtaker, not an identified terminal developer/owner -- the 2016 RFP for that role appears never to have concluded); no concrete recent step (nothing found since 2016, target in-service date lapsed).
watch_for: Any RdK/Curacao government announcement naming a selected LNG-terminal developer/operator for Bullen Bay, or a gas-supply component attached to a refinery-reopening deal.
notes: Curacao has zero GEM LNG rows (confirmed coverage gap). A low-detail 'Curacao CNG-LNG Terminal feasibility study' document (scribd.com/document/660123711) also circulates but failed url_verifier (no LNG content retrievable) and adds no sponsor/date beyond the 2016 RFP already captured here -- not cited.
